parts.text: The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A grotesque disfigured old man with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin with age spots, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a large ear with a fat hanging lobe, thick neck, hunched broad shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Head type: a huge tall lumpy dome skull with dents and bumps, like the master reference, ruddy red-pink clay skin, a greasy black comb-over, raised blue clay veins on the forehead, his visible ear is mostly torn away, only a ragged bloody stump of ear left with jagged torn edges and dried blood, a crude crown of jagged yellowed bone shards and splintered wooden stakes standing up around his head, bound tightly to his skull with thick coils of frayed rope. No mask: a gaunt creature face with a huge lipless mouth full of rows of jagged needle teeth, a flat slitted nose, small glinting black eyes and wiry tufts of hair. Wearing a grimy one-piece black work jumpsuit with a small blank torn cloth chest patch (no lettering on it), his right fist grips a long rusty machete dripping blood; his LEFT fist tightly grips a rusty pitchfork by its long wooden handle, held upright at his side with the rusty tines rising above his shoulder beside his head, carried in his hand, not strapped to his back. The inside of a grimy walk-in meat freezer: frosted steel walls and a frozen floor, rows of big rusty meat hooks hanging from an overhead rail, raw bloody animal carcasses and sides of meat hanging from the hooks, icy mist and cold blue light, sculpted as a miniature claymation diorama in matte plasticine, softly out of focus behind him, no signs, no lettering. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, his body is in three-quarter view and his head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Both hands are full and both are tight clenched fists, knuckles toward the camera: the right fist grips the held weapon, the left fist grips the second weapon by its handle as described. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora
